bullets.title: NVDA Q2 FY2027 earnings beat: $96.2B revenue, 70% FY28 growth guide
bullets.body: NVIDIA posted record Q2 revenue of $96.2B (+106% YoY), crushing consensus of $92.2–$92.4B, with data center hitting $89B (+117%). More importantly, CFO Colette Kress guided FY2028 revenue growth of ~70% YoY—vs. street expectations of ~45%—while noting supply constraints are the limiting factor. SpaceX AI adopts Vera CPU; AWS commits to 2M additional GPUs through 2027–2028. Stock rallied 7–8% in after-hours.

bullets.title: NVDA's Hugging Face acquisition reportedly finalized at $12.9B
bullets.body: Multiple sources including The Information and Bloomberg reported NVIDIA agreed to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.9B, expanding its open-source AI model repository and developer ecosystem. The deal appeared to be confirmed by NVIDIA's CFO in earnings call context around the same time.

bullets.title: Marvell beats Q2 but guides Q3 above consensus; stock drops on elevated expectations
bullets.body: MRVL posted Q2 FY2027 revenue of $2.74B (+37% YoY), beating $2.71B consensus, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 vs. $0.93 expected. Q3 guidance of $3.15B (+15% QoQ) topped consensus $3.03B. Despite solid results, the stock fell 5–8% after-hours as investor expectations had been set very high; FY27 revenue guide raised to ~$12B (+45% YoY). CXL adoption and optical interconnect momentum were key takeaways from the earnings call.

bullets.title: Meta agrees to $16–18B settlement on youth social media harm; legal overhang cleared
bullets.body: Meta reached a settlement with 48 U.S. states over allegations that Facebook and Instagram harmed children, agreeing to pay up to $16.68B over 10 years and implement screen-time limits and parental controls. META will accrue ~$10B in Q3 2026 as a one-time legal charge. Analysts viewed the outcome as far less severe than worst-case risk (estimated up to $1.4T), and the stock rallied ~4% in premarket on the news.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh hawkish at Jackson Hole; September hike probability surges to ~50%
bullets.body: Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair struck a hawkish tone, stating inflation 'hasn't been convincing,' calling out financial conditions that are 'hard-pressed to describe as restrictive,' and signaling more work may be needed. Markets repriced: September hike odds jumped from ~30–36% pre-speech to ~50–60% on futures/prediction markets. The 2-year Treasury yield spiked to 4.348%; the yield curve flattened sharply.

bullets.title: Warsh speech triggers sharp post-Jackson Hole market repricing; stocks reverse
bullets.body: US stocks fell on Warsh's hawkish stance, with Nasdaq down ~0.5% on Friday. Options market showed bullish/call stances fading across both bonds and equities post-speech. CME FedWatch priced 57% September hike probability. Chicago PMI collapsed to 47.1 vs. 57.9 expected—a massive miss—adding to economic-data confusion but Warsh's message dominated.

bullets.title: PCE inflation sticky; July core PCE +3.3% YoY, headline beats at +3.7%
bullets.body: July personal consumption expenditure data showed headline PCE at +0.2% MoM (vs. +0.1% est.) and +3.7% YoY, above 3.6% forecast. Core PCE held at 3.3%, matching estimates. The data kept markets on edge for a rate hike and reinforced Warsh's hawkish messaging ahead of Jackson Hole. Services ex-housing inflation remained elevated at +3.8% YoY.

bullets.title: OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC debuts at Hot Chips; claims 1.5–2x efficiency edge over Nvidia Rubin
bullets.body: OpenAI announced its Jalapeño custom inference ASIC at Hot Chips 2026, developed with Broadcom, claiming 1.5–2x better throughput per watt vs. Nvidia GB300/Rubin and 1.7–3.6x lower latency. Co-designed with AI assistance, the chip reached tape-out in roughly nine months vs. a typical 3-year cycle. Analysts debated whether this meaningfully threatens Nvidia's near-term dominance or pressures the CUDA moat; most see it as a 2027–2028 production-scale story.

bullets.title: TSMC Q2 earnings strong; Moody's raises outlook to positive; $3.75B turnover record
bullets.body: TSMC was the most actively traded stock with $3.75B in turnover as the week began. Moody's upgraded its outlook to positive citing strong AI demand. Q2 employee profit-sharing payouts surged 50%+ YoY to $1.14B. Vera Rubin first systems shipped to Microsoft; Kioxia planning ¥1T new fab in Japan, signaling continued advanced packaging demand.

bullets.title: Tim Cook steps down as Apple CEO; John Ternus takes over Aug. 31
bullets.body: Tim Cook officially steps down as Apple CEO effective August 31, with hardware engineering chief John Ternus succeeding him. Under Cook, Apple grew from ~$350B to >$4T market cap. Apple also launched M6 chip (TSMC 2nm) Mac mini and M5 Ultra Mac Studio during the week, and raised Apple TV+ subscription price to $14.99/month. iPhone 18 event set for September 9.

bullets.title: SK Hynix CEO: Memory shortage to persist through end of 2030; DRAM prices at 5-year highs
bullets.body: SK Hynix CEO dismissed oversupply concerns, forecasting tight memory through 2030 as AI-driven demand far outpaces capacity additions. Analysts noted DRAM prices now equivalent to 620 grams of gold per kilogram of chips—up from 120g equivalent in 2023 trough. Memory cost surges are being passed through to devices; non-flagship smartphone memory BOM now exceeds premium chipset costs.

bullets.title: AMD upgrades and market share gains; Intel 18A yields ahead of targets
bullets.body: Raymond James upgraded AMD to Strong Buy with $641 PT (from $565) citing server CPU market growing to $201B by 2030 at 44% CAGR. AMD server CPU market share crossed 30% for first time and 46.4% of server CPUs. Intel's 14A D0 process tracking ahead of yield targets per DB conference disclosures; 18A-P achieves 30% frequency gain at 0.5V on Diamond Rapids silicon.

bullets.title: Salesforce surges 20%+ on earnings; ClaudeForce partnership announced
bullets.body: CRM posted Q2 FY27 revenue of $11.35B, beating consensus, with non-GAAP EPS of $5.90. The stock surged 19–22% for its best day since August 2020. Alongside earnings, Salesforce announced 'ClaudeForce' - a partnership with Anthropic integrating Claude AI into the Salesforce platform, with beta launching September 2026.

bullets.title: CrowdStrike beats Q2; +10% in after-hours; cybersecurity as AI bottleneck trade
bullets.body: CrowdStrike reported Q2 revenue of $1.47B (+2.1% vs $1.44B est.) with net new ARR of $332.8M smashing the $285.9M estimate. Raised FY2027 guidance. One trader's thread identified cybersecurity as 'the next $1T AI bottleneck' with CRWD positioned as the control plane for agentic AI. Fal.Con conference next week features Jensen Huang as keynote.

bullets.title: US-Canada trade war escalates; 50% tariffs on autos, steel from Jan 1, 2027
bullets.body: Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles, auto parts, and steel effective January 1, 2027 via Truth Social, declaring 'Canada will be treated like a state no longer.' Canada retaliated with up to 50% tariffs on ~$20B of US goods effective September 8, targeting steel, aluminum, appliances, and farm equipment. Ontario Premier Ford threatened to cut electricity and critical minerals exports to the US.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz geopolitical risk persists; Iran-Oman shipping corridor talks
bullets.body: Commodity vessel traffic through the Strait fell to sub-5 ships vs. a 15-vessel 10-day average. Oman and Iran discussed a temporary shipping corridor and joint mine-clearing project, driving oil down 3–4%. CENTCOM reported clearing Iranian mines and 82 vessel redirections. White House confirmed no new Iran strikes planned near-term while Bessent unveiled 'Operation Economic Outcast' sanctioning 60+ Iran-linked entities.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler debt and off-balance-sheet AI exposure drawing credit market scrutiny
bullets.body: Broadcom CDS hit all-time highs (+5bp); NVDA CDS also at record-wide levels. Goldman Sachs flagged hyperscaler off-balance-sheet AI liabilities reaching $3.1T, up $1.3T in three months. Goldman traders noted credit asking questions that equity markets haven't priced. The circular AI financing structure—Nvidia guaranteeing AI cloud revenue to enable data center debt—drew significant analytical attention.

bullets.title: Nancy Pelosi discloses up to $12M in Bloom Energy and $1.5M in Intel
bullets.body: Pelosi filed disclosures showing purchases of 15,000 shares of BE and 10,000 shares of INTC, plus call options worth up to $5M in BE (expiry 6/17/27) and $500K in INTC. BE rallied ~10–12% on copytrader momentum. Several fintwit accounts noted Pelosi's purchases aligned with data center power and AI infrastructure themes.

bullets.title: Kioxia-SanDisk commit $31B to Japan NAND expansion; semiconductor capex cycle accelerating
bullets.body: Kioxia and SanDisk announced $31B+ in Japan capacity investments through 2032, with Kioxia separately planning ¥1 trillion for a new Iwate fab. SemiAnalysis flagged NVDA Rubin Ultra HBM content downgrade to 192GB 8-Hi vs. 1TB originally previewed. WFE model raised to $140–165B in 2026 and $195–250B by 2028.

bullets.title: Global bond market stress: 30Y Treasury at 5.21%, Japan 10Y at 30-year highs
bullets.body: US 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.21% intraday before easing. Japan's 10-year JGB yield surpassed 2.9% (highest since 1996) and 2-year JGB demand hit weakest since 2016. German 10-year Bund yields at 15-year highs. Gold surged to $4,700+ and Bitcoin broke $80K as debasement trades accelerated. Treasury Secretary Bessent hinted at using the $935B TGA to fund expanded bond buybacks.
